title: AI Body Swap
summary: Free AI body swap: keep a character's face and put it on a new body, outfit or pose, from a knight or an astronaut to a marble statue. Free to try.
body_markdown:
### How do I do an AI body swap?


Add a clear portrait as a reference image, then ask for the same person in a new body, outfit, pose and setting, naming the face features to keep, such as the hair, eyes, beard or any marks.


### What is the difference between a body swap and a face swap?


A face swap puts a new face on an existing photo and keeps that photo's body, while a body swap keeps the person's face and draws a new body, outfit and pose around it.


### Is there a free AI body swap?


Yes. Flick is free to start: the free plan gives 100 credits every day with no credit card, and GPT Image 2.6, which made the body swaps here, costs 5 credits an image at its default settings.


### How do I keep the face the same in an AI body swap?


Start from a sharp, front-facing portrait, add it as a reference, and repeat the face features to keep in every prompt; GPT Image 2.6 takes up to 10 reference images, so you can add more than one photo of the face.


### Can I put my face on a different outfit or costume?


Yes. Add your photo as a reference and describe the outfit, such as knight's armour, a spacesuit or a chef's jacket, with a full figure framing, so the whole costume is in the picture.


### Can a body swap change the type of character?


Yes. Ask for the same person as a 3D cartoon, an anime character or a marble statue, and list the features to carry over, such as the beard, hair and earring, so the new character keeps the identity.


### Can I turn a body swap into a video?


Yes. Generate the still first, then use it as the start frame of an image to video model in Flick and describe one simple action, asking it to keep the face exactly as in the image.
